hypothesis: Using 48 threads per CTA instead of 256 may expose more schedulable CTAs while preserving one thread per target, but it also leaves 16 lanes idle in each CTA’s second warp and may increase CTA overhead. Measure rather than assume a speedup.
notes: Only launch geometry changes; the kernel’s traversal, force equations, and memory behavior remain unchanged. Supplied search results show a correct 256-thread baseline at 0.00185264 s, 12-thread CTAs at 0.00179779 s, 24-thread CTAs at 0.00180446 s, and 1-thread CTAs at 0.00383506 s. These are search measurements, not independent confirmation; the 48-thread configuration is unmeasured. Validate all supported sizes before comparing official timings.
transformations: Set block and items_per_block to 48 and retain shared_memory_bytes at 0, preserving the exact JSON key set.
